1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to disburse full amount of compensation to the petitioner in terms of report dated 17.8.2023, with interest, excluding Rs. 5,46,180/-, which already stood paid.

2. It appears that IHB Limited, a joint venture company of Indian Oil Corporation Limited,
Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited, needed certain land for laying LPG pipeline and in that connection, acquisition was made on 3.3.2021 for use of land 12 meters in width under the provisions of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 and the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

1 of the land covering an area of 1.2116 hectares was declared on 23.12.2022 by the competent authority, followed by a supplementary award dated 10.5.2023 in respect of the standing crops over the said land and a separate award dated 5.3.2024 with respect to the standing trees over the said land.

sentences.text: In the instant petition, the dispute is confined to the claim of compensation in respect of the standing trees.
The case of the petitioner is that she has been paid only a sum of Rs. 5,46,180/- and not the entire amount and she is also not being informed of the manner of calculation of the said amount.
The petitioner has placed reliance on a report dated 17.8.2023 in contending that as per the report, she is entitled to a much higher amount as compensation for trees standing over the land.
4. A counter affidavit has been filed by the competent authority, i.e. IHB Limited (respondent no. 6).
The said respondent has indicated the manner in which compensation amount has been calculated and paid to the petitioner.

According to the calculation sheet, a total sum of Rs. 9,70,370/- was awarded as compensation for 202 trees standing over the the land and the share of the petitioner and her husband Ranvijay Singh, has been shown as Rs. 5,46,180/-.
Thus, according to respondent no. 6, she has been paid full amount of compensation in terms of the award dated 5.3.2024.
5. Counsel for the petitioner is not in a position to dispute the calculation disclosed by respondent no. 6.
He however, submits that the compensation awarded is inadequate and as per the report dated 17.8.2023, the petitioner is entitled to a much higher amount as compensation for the standing trees.

6. Sri Anand Tiwari, learned counsel for respondent no. 6, submits that in case the petitioner is disputing the quantum of compensation, her remedy is by way of reference to the District Judge in terms of Section 10(2) of the Act of 1962, read with Rule 5 of the Rules framed under the said Act.

7. Section 10(2) stipulates as follows: -
"10(2) If the amount of compensation determined by the competent authority under sub-section (1) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount of compensation shall, on application by either of the parties to the District Judge within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land or any part thereof is situated, be determined by that District Judge."
8.
We find considerable force in the submission.

Since the issue involves determination of questions of fact and remedy is provided under the Act itself, therefore, we are not inclined to examine the issue under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
9. The petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to avail the statutory remedy, if so advised.
(Anish Kumar Gupta, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
